chapter: Looking back, big bands and sidemen
title: Big band experience as a period piece
summary: New big band players aren't realistic; Richie Cole called big band experience a period piece, and Herman says a band working every night beats one that rehearses weekly.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well, that's hard to foresee, what changes might appear in the future for people who want to continue with bands.
Yeah, well, there are more and more new people involved in the band -- big band field today, but I don't feel that they're really being realistic about it, because in
They're feel we're losing the chance to be a part of something that they will never be able to do in any other kind of music, or get done in small groups.

What you mention brings to mind a comment that was made by young Richie Cole, the alto player. And reflecting about his experience with Buddy Rich's band, he said, 'You know, a big band experience is like a period piece.' That was very good, because it's there, and if you don't pick it up, it's gone.

That's right, and you may never have that opportunity. Because, the fact, as I've always truly thought, that a group that stays together, even for a matter of months, and works every night, is a much better group than one that stays together five years and meets once or twice a week.
Uh-huh, I see what you're saying.
